## Verdict
needs-revision

## Concerns
- `claim-1` does not justify that \((i,j,p,c)=(2,2,3,4)\) is the smallest untested case or explain the invariant’s expected information gain.
- The identification of the computed Pieri row lattice with \(A_+J\) is not proved.
- Artifact `a3ad933b835c991bc8edccec918dce17c0e4594e4d1d4281e32946dd7e508ece` used `requireSmithWitnesses=false`; therefore the reported Smith forms, ranks, and torsion claims lack persisted independently checkable witnesses.
- The requested target is explicitly reported as not established. No all-case conclusion is inferred, and withholding pattern extraction is appropriate while review objections remain unresolved.

## Unresolved certificates
- [proof-attempt] Enumerate all smaller admissible genuinely two-sided parameter cases under an explicit ordering, identify their accepted coverage or conjugation equivalence, and justify why this asymmetric case and the integral indecomposable quotient maximize expected information gain.
- [proof-attempt] Prove for \(A=\Lambda/I_{6,5}\) that \(J=\bigoplus_{22\subseteq\lambda\subseteq5^6}\mathbb Z\bar s_\lambda\), \(A_+=(h_1,\ldots,h_5)\), and the complete displayed Pieri rows present each graded component of \(A_+J\).
- [computation] Rerun the exact same input with `requireSmithWitnesses=true`, persisting degreewise Smith operation logs or \(U M V=D\) witnesses, unimodularity checks, full stdout, stderr, exit status, and stable digests.
